argument_summary: The current record supports a narrow defense of certification as an operationally ready, monitored, and reversible release decision: aggregate readiness cleared by 2.1 points, rehearsal showed no severity-one incidents, and rollout begins at 6% with rollback and monitoring-oriented controls. The same record does not support a clean claim that rollout controls fully cure the model-card issue, because the small-business onboarding segment remains exposed, the rollout gate does not exclude it, and the draft risk acceptance is incomplete and unsigned. The appropriate interpretation is therefore weak support for certification with the disclosure-governance gap explicitly preserved in the packet, rather than escalation based on an overstated claim of full policy satisfaction.
claims_about_policy: The admissible evidence supports distinguishing operational readiness from full policy closure. Aggregate readiness, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, rollback capability, and monitoring are relevant to launch safety and reversibility. But under the stated policy, those controls do not by themselves remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed unless approved risk acceptance covers that exposure. On this record, certification is defensible only as a monitored, reversible launch decision with an unresolved disclosure-governance limitation clearly recorded, not as clean compliance with the disclosure predicate.
claims_about_business_cost: No separate business-cost claim is required to resolve the audit concern on this record.
concessions: The small-business onboarding segment remains below target on long-context onboarding support and is still exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
The rollout gate does not exclude the affected segment.
The draft risk acceptance is unsigned and does not address the exposed segment.
The present record does not support saying rollout controls alone satisfy the disclosure policy predicate.
The certification case is weak and should not be framed as fully policy-satisfied.
